rows.choose: Relational SQL, joins and transactions with a supported managed engine. Choose engine, edition and workload compatibility first.
rows.operations: AWS manages underlying infrastructure and supported backups/patching; you own schema, queries, grants, maintenance choices and capacity. Classic Multi-AZ has a non-readable synchronous standby; read replicas are asynchronous.
rows.watch: Multi-AZ DB clusters instead have a writer plus two readable replicas across three AZs. Backup retention is up to 35 days; restore creates a new endpoint. TLS, KMS and database authorization solve separate layers.

rows.choose: MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible relational workloads needing distributed storage, readers, Serverless v2 or eligible global deployments.
rows.operations: Storage copies span three AZs independently of compute. Writer, reader, instance and custom endpoints select different destinations; up to 15 readers. Provisioned instances or supported ACU ranges determine compute.
rows.watch: Reader endpoint balances new connections, not queries; with no readers it can reach the writer. Global replication is asynchronous; write forwarding still commits at the primary. Version/Region limits and pause eligibility matter.

rows.choose: Pool and reuse eligible RDS/Aurora connections for bursty applications and controlled failover.
rows.operations: Private endpoint; validate supported engine/version, VPC routing, security groups and configured authentication. Measure database connections, client connections and pinned sessions.
rows.watch: Session state can pin connections and reduce multiplexing. Extra read-only proxy endpoints target eligible Aurora readers; a proxy neither scales SQL capacity indefinitely nor serves arbitrary RDS replicas.

rows.choose: Managed key-value/document access with known partition/sort-key patterns, conditional writes and supported transactions.
rows.operations: Choose on-demand or provisioned capacity. Query uses partition-key equality; GSIs enable alternate keys. Regional table/LSI reads can be strong; GSIs remain eventual. PITR restores to a new table.
rows.watch: 400-KB items; 100 actions/4 MB per transaction. Filters run after reads. TTL deletion is asynchronous. MREC and MRSC global tables have different consistency, topology and feature support; hot keys can still throttle.

rows.choose: Accelerate supported eventually consistent DynamoDB reads with a DynamoDB-aware cache client.
rows.operations: Regional VPC cluster; primary plus replicas, up to 11 nodes. Plan at least three nodes across AZs for production availability. Separate item/query caches have configurable TTL, default five minutes.
rows.watch: Strong/transactional reads pass through without populating cache. Writes through DAX do not invalidate Query/Scan results. Direct or remote-Region writes can leave cached data stale; it is not a generic SQL/session cache.

rows.choose: Application-managed caching, sessions, counters and supported data structures; choose node-based or Serverless explicitly.
rows.operations: Application owns keys, serialization, cache-aside/write strategy, TTL, invalidation and fallback. Replication/failover protect availability; sharding adds capacity. Benchmark hits, misses, evictions and source load.
rows.watch: Check the selected engine/deployment: eligible node-based Valkey supports optional synchronous/asynchronous Multi-AZ-log durability; it is not generic Redis AOF. Eligible Valkey 9+ Serverless public endpoints require IAM and TLS 1.3. Replica freshness and application expiry still need explicit handling.

rows.choose: Simple distributed key/value caching where the application can refill lost data.
rows.operations: Distribute keys and manage miss/stampede behavior. Multithreading and horizontal distribution differ from Valkey/Redis replication and failover.
rows.watch: Node-based Memcached has no snapshot backup; Serverless Memcached supports snapshots. Do not infer durable primary-database semantics or another engine’s feature set.

rows.choose: A compatible in-memory primary database when durability is required rather than a disposable cache alone.
rows.operations: Multi-AZ transactional log supports durability and recovery. Select supported engine/version and validate application/client compatibility, network and access controls.
rows.watch: Compare its exact durability, write latency, API, recovery and cost contract with the selected ElastiCache configuration, including eligible durable node-based Valkey. Do not infer identical features from a compatible client API.

title: Search, document, graph and time-series services

rows.choose: Full-text search, log exploration and derived analytical indexes. Compare managed domains with Serverless collections.
rows.operations: Plan mappings, shards/capacity, ingestion, retention and access. Serverless network, encryption and data-access policies are separate from caller IAM permissions.
rows.watch: An asynchronous search view can lag the source. Backfill, duplicates, deletions, rejected records and reconciliation need explicit handling. Dashboards is the presentation layer, not the ingest engine.

rows.choose: Managed document workloads that pass validation against the supported MongoDB-compatible API.
rows.operations: Validate drivers, operators, indexes, transaction behavior and connection handling. Instance-based clusters support readers; Standard and I/O-Optimized change the I/O cost model.
rows.watch: Compatibility is not engine identity. Up to 15 readers; storage maximum depends on engine/configuration (eligible engine 8+ 256 TiB, earlier 128 TiB). Include readers, backup, I/O and transfer in cost estimates.

rows.choose: Highly connected graph traversals, knowledge graphs and relationship-heavy fraud/recommendation queries.
rows.operations: Choose property-graph Gremlin/openCypher or RDF/SPARQL semantics. Plan private connectivity, IAM/database access, TLS/KMS, query design and recovery.
rows.watch: Graph access is a distinct data model; it does not replace a document API or relational joins without redesign. Validate supported query language and chosen Neptune product/deployment.

rows.choose: Existing eligible customers: SQL time-series analysis with memory/magnetic retention and time-oriented functions.
rows.operations: Model time, dimensions and measures; validate late arrivals, retention, scheduled queries, multi-measure records and supported ingestion integrations.
rows.watch: Closed to new customers on 20 June 2025. Existing eligible payer accounts continue. Historical performance/price ratios are not guarantees; preserve this availability qualification.

rows.choose: Evaluate a current time-series alternative with the selected InfluxDB product/version and workload.
rows.operations: Validate query APIs/languages, endpoint/client compatibility, supported deployment size, retention, ingestion, backup and monitoring for the chosen offering.
rows.watch: It is not a drop-in LiveAnalytics API or memory/magnetic-tier implementation. InfluxDB 2 and 3 offerings differ; verify actual integrations before migration.

title: Supporting services in the database architecture

rows.choose: Supported full-load and change-data-capture migration paths.
rows.operations: Check source/target compatibility, source logging/permissions, replication capacity, lag and reconciliation. Fence writes and validate controlled cutover.
rows.watch: CDC is not zero-loss magic or a complete backup strategy. Schema/extension conversion and application compatibility need separate work.

rows.choose: Objects, supported import/export, snapshots and metadata-index patterns.
rows.operations: Use bucket policies, IAM, encryption/KMS and supported engine integrations. DynamoDB can hold queryable object metadata; S3 holds the object.
rows.watch: S3 is not a mounted database filesystem. Object events may repeat or arrive out of order; maintain and reconcile metadata aggregates.

rows.choose: Event processing, supported stream consumers and bursty database clients.
rows.operations: Choose workload role, private network path, concurrency and idempotent retry/checkpoint behavior. Use a compatible proxy for connection pressure when appropriate.
rows.watch: A VPC attachment alone does not grant database access. Repeated records and connection storms require deliberate handling.

rows.choose: Replayable streaming, including supported DynamoDB change capture.
rows.operations: Choose capacity and retention (supported 24 hours to 365 days); checkpoint and monitor consumer lag.
rows.watch: DynamoDB capture can duplicate/reorder changes. Native DynamoDB Streams instead retains 24 hours with per-item ordering; consumers can still repeat processing.

rows.choose: Buffered delivery into supported storage/search destinations.
rows.operations: Configure IAM, transformation, buffering, destination security, failed-record backup and delivery monitoring.
rows.watch: Buffering adds latency. It is a delivery service, not identical to a replayable Kinesis stream or an immediate per-record query path.

rows.choose: Metrics, alarms, logs and supported database-load diagnosis.
rows.operations: Correlate load/waits/SQL with CPU, memory, swap and Enhanced Monitoring evidence; validate log retention and delivery routes.
rows.watch: CloudTrail API evidence does not replace SQL audit logs. Subscription/Lambda and Firehose delivery have different latency/retry contracts.

rows.choose: Audit supported database and infrastructure API activity.
rows.operations: Configure trails/event selection, retention, access and protected destinations; correlate identity and time with operational evidence.
rows.watch: Do not assume every SQL statement is a control-plane event. Use the engine’s supported audit/query logs for that requirement.

rows.choose: Deliver supported RDS event notifications to subscribed consumers.
rows.operations: Configure event categories, subscription confirmation, target policy and monitoring of downstream delivery.
rows.watch: Notifications complement alarms and query logs; they do not diagnose every slow query or provide a full data audit.

rows.choose: Protect eligible database, snapshot and backup data at rest with encryption keys.
rows.operations: Plan key policy, grants, cross-account/cross-Region recovery and key retention. Test restore permissions before an incident.
rows.watch: Encryption at rest does not supply TLS or database grants. Disabling/deleting a required key can block recovery.

rows.choose: Store and rotate supported credentials used by database clients, proxies and Data API.
rows.operations: Scope retrieval/rotation permissions and KMS access; refresh application connections and validate rotation workflows.
rows.watch: A stored secret is not automatic database authorization. Rotation needs compatible database/app behavior and error handling.

rows.choose: Authorize AWS APIs and eligible IAM database-login requests.
rows.operations: Use least-privilege roles; supported IAM DB auth requires rds-db:connect plus database user setup and TLS. Login tokens last 15 minutes.
rows.watch: Token expiry does not terminate an already authenticated session. Control-plane IAM and SQL/database grants remain distinct.

rows.choose: DNS-based application endpoint cutover and validated regional routing.
rows.operations: Account for health signals, DNS TTL, client caches and reconnect behavior; test promotion and endpoint changes together.
rows.watch: DNS does not promote a replica or automatically redirect DynamoDB SDK operations. Fence the former writer before controlled recovery.

rows.choose: Managed API front door for data-backed applications.
rows.operations: Validate authentication, throttling, integration timeout, payload and downstream database/concurrency limits.
rows.watch: Historic default quotas are not universal throughput guarantees. Cache misses and backend hot partitions still constrain the full request path.

rows.choose: Edge distribution and eligible response caching ahead of application origins.
rows.operations: Select cache keys/TTL, authorization handling, origin protection and observability for the specific workload.
rows.watch: Do not cache private tenant data under a shared key. Edge capacity does not eliminate API, compute or database bottlenecks.

rows.choose: Buffer asynchronous work when latency and processing semantics allow decoupling.
rows.operations: Configure visibility timeout, retries, dead-letter handling, idempotency and consumer capacity.
rows.watch: A queue is not unbounded capacity or a synchronous database accelerator. Backlogs and downstream write limits still require monitoring.

rows.choose: Authenticate devices and route supported telemetry toward time-series processing.
rows.operations: Validate device identity, policies, rule actions, payload formats, event time and downstream retry/error handling.
rows.watch: A producer/rule integration must match the selected time-series service; connectors are not interchangeable.

rows.service: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
rows.choose: Stateful stream transforms, windows and supported event-time processing.
rows.operations: Plan checkpoints, state recovery, capacity, source/sink permissions and late-event behavior.
rows.watch: A processing engine is not the durable query store. Validate sink compatibility and exactly-once boundaries end to end.

rows.choose: Supported BI visualization over prepared analytical data.
rows.operations: Validate connector, dataset refresh/direct-query behavior, row-level access and dashboard permissions.
rows.watch: A dashboard does not define ingestion correctness or source freshness; enforce tenant visibility and understand refresh lag.

rows.choose: Supported machine-learning consumption/analysis of prepared data.
rows.operations: Validate data extraction, format, roles, encryption and pipeline reproducibility.
rows.watch: A historical integration illustration is not proof every time-series product exposes the same connector.

rows.choose: Private database placement and validated application/database reachability.
rows.operations: Check subnets, routes, DNS, security groups, port and client connection paths; separate private AWS API access from database protocol access.
rows.watch: Private placement does not grant SQL permissions or guarantee egress. A database endpoint is not the same as an AWS control-plane API endpoint.

rows.choose: OS/database control or a supported migration destination whose requirements exceed a managed service contract.
rows.operations: You own host/database patching, storage, backup, replication, failover, licensing and monitoring. Validate consistent seed and catch-up before cutover.
rows.watch: An RDS backup/export path is not universally reversible. Supported Oracle RMAN exports can target self-managed recovery; arbitrary RMAN restores into managed RDS are not supported.

rows.choose: Supported Kafka-based telemetry or ingestion pipelines.
rows.operations: Plan broker/serverless operating model, client authentication, topics, retention, consumer lag and compatible downstream connectors.
rows.watch: A supported Kafka source is not automatic compatibility with every Timestream offering. Validate delivery semantics, event time, duplicates and reconciliation.

rows.choose: Managed dashboards over compatible data sources.
rows.operations: Configure workspace identity, data-source permissions, supported query integration and user access.
rows.watch: Dashboard freshness follows source ingestion and query behavior. Grafana does not create source-data durability or tenant isolation automatically.

rows.choose: AWS-native orchestration with task definitions, services and finite tasks.
rows.operations: Choose compute independently: EC2, supported managed capacity or Fargate. A service maintains desired tasks; task and execution roles separate runtime AWS calls from startup actions.
rows.watch: Service scaling changes tasks, not automatically an unmanaged EC2 fleet. awsvpc needs IP target groups; bridge can use instance/dynamic-port targets. Secrets injected at startup need task replacement after rotation.

rows.choose: Managed regional Kubernetes control plane with Kubernetes APIs/ecosystem.
rows.operations: Choose managed/self-managed EC2, supported Auto Mode or Fargate. Kubernetes RBAC/access entries authorize cluster actions; IRSA/Pod Identity authorize workload AWS APIs.
rows.watch: Worker, driver, network and identity compatibility remain your design. The EKS management PrivateLink endpoint is not the Kubernetes API private endpoint. Namespace alone is not a hard tenant boundary.

rows.choose: Run compatible ECS tasks without operating worker hosts.
rows.operations: awsvpc is required; select supported CPU/memory/OS/storage and private startup reachability. Execution role covers supported image pull/log/secret actions.
rows.watch: Task IAM role is separate. Private tasks may need ECR API + registry, S3 layers, Logs and Secrets paths. Fargate Spot interruptions need tolerant tasks; no automatic On-Demand fallback guarantee.

rows.choose: Run supported Pods selected by Fargate profiles without managing worker nodes.
rows.operations: Match namespace/labels, scheduling, supported resource shape and workload identity. Eligible EFS static provisioning can supply persistent shared storage.
rows.watch: No Fargate Spot, arbitrary DaemonSets, privileged workloads, EBS Pod volumes or Pod Identity agent path. Do not assume feature parity with ECS Fargate or EC2 nodes.

rows.choose: Host control, instance selection and workloads that need compatible host-level capabilities.
rows.operations: Plan AZ spread, AMI/OS patching, agents, bootstrap, IAM, capacity and draining. ECS capacity providers or compatible EKS node autoscaling coordinate host capacity.
rows.watch: Host scaling and task/Pod scaling are separate loops. Running two tasks on one host is not independent host availability; Spot and drain behavior need testing.

rows.choose: Store OCI/container images and distribute eligible artifacts by digest.
rows.operations: Combine caller/repository policy and network access. Use digest-pinned release records, scan configuration, lifecycle previews and deliberate cross-Region/account replication.
rows.watch: Scanning does not patch. Replication does not deploy applications or mirror deletions/settings automatically; historical content needs deliberate backfill. Retention must preserve rollback images.

rows.choose: Enhanced ECR vulnerability scanning for supported OS and language packages.
rows.operations: Configure eligible repositories and scan frequency; route findings to triage, rebuild, rescan and deployment decisions.
rows.watch: Basic and Enhanced scanning have different coverage/reporting contracts. A finding-free image is not a guarantee of secure configuration or runtime behavior.

rows.choose: Evaluate simplified image-to-application provisioning in your AWS account, including App Runner migration.
rows.operations: Provide image and required IAM roles; ECS provisions supported Fargate service, ALB, scaling and networking. Underlying resources remain visible and billable.
rows.watch: No separate Express Mode fee does not mean free infrastructure. Validate private dependencies, networking, ownership and rollout/rollback parity.

rows.choose: Existing eligible customers: managed code/image web-service deployment, HTTPS, health and scaling.
rows.operations: Outbound private access uses a VPC connector. Private incoming access uses separate endpoint/ingress-connection configuration; public ingress is an alternative.
rows.watch: Closed to new customers 31 March 2026; no planned new features. AWS recommends evaluating ECS Express Mode. VPC egress alone does not make ingress private.

rows.choose: Regional ECS management with tasks on supported customer-operated external hosts.
rows.operations: Install/register ECS and Systems Manager agents, scope IAM and use EXTERNAL launch type. You own hardware, host patching, capacity, local security and recovery.
rows.watch: Management requires regional connectivity; already-running tasks can continue during a disconnect. bridge/host/none only; no awsvpc or supported ECS service load balancing/discovery on external instances.

rows.choose: Customer-operated local Kubernetes control plane on supported infrastructure.
rows.operations: Prepare local registry/dependencies and lifecycle operations for connected, disconnected or air-gapped operation. Optional Connector provides console visibility.
rows.watch: It is not a managed regional EKS control plane. You retain upgrades, backups, security, capacity and recovery; disconnection does not require switching to bare EKS Distro.

rows.choose: Kubernetes distribution components when the customer needs to assemble and operate the platform.
rows.operations: Own control-plane installation, infrastructure, upgrades, compatibility, backup and recovery. Distinguish distribution packaging from the EKS Anywhere lifecycle tooling.
rows.watch: Not a hosted EKS service and not the sole way to operate disconnected. Assess operational capability before choosing this lower-level contract.

rows.service: ECS Managed Instances · ECS compute option
rows.choose: EC2 hardware selection with supported infrastructure provisioning, scaling, patching and maintenance managed by ECS.
rows.operations: Use a compatible capacity provider, task definition, infrastructure role and instance profile. Validate Linux/architecture, resource requirements, networking and workload compatibility.
rows.watch: It is distinct from self-managed EC2 and Fargate. A capacity-provider strategy cannot mix Managed Instances, ASG and Fargate provider types; compute management does not remove application security/availability responsibilities.

rows.choose: Extend managed Kubernetes operations into supported compute, networking, load balancing and block-storage functions.
rows.operations: Use supported NodePools/NodeClasses and workload settings; AWS manages appliance-like nodes and platform components. Plan Pod/NodePool disruption budgets and compatible identity/storage.
rows.watch: It is not EKS Fargate. Nodes have no direct SSH/SSM access and have a maximum 21-day lifetime; blocking disruption settings can require intervention. Workload policies and data recovery remain your responsibility.

rows.choose: Discover registered endpoints/attributes through supported DNS or API queries.
rows.operations: Maintain namespace, services, registrations and applicable health checks. Clients connect directly to returned backends; health filtering and TTL affect discovery.
rows.watch: Not an inline proxy, load balancer or tunnel. DNS fail-open/client caching and DiscoverInstances filters differ; registration alone does not authorize a tenant.

rows.choose: Managed task proxies and consistent ECS service-to-service names within supported namespaces.
rows.operations: Configure discovery aliases/ports, namespace membership and proxy resources. Routes/security groups must permit traffic. Supported TLS uses Private CA, infrastructure role and managed certificate secrets.
rows.watch: One namespace per service; compatible same-Region clusters/shared accounts require supported setup. It is not automatic cross-Region networking or every legacy mesh traffic-control feature.

rows.choose: Application-layer connectivity and explicit authorization across supported VPC/account service boundaries.
rows.operations: Configure service networks, associations/sharing, listeners, targets and health. IAM authentication combines auth policy, caller permission and signed requests.
rows.watch: Network association is not permission. Validate supported target/protocol behavior, security paths and access logs; connectivity does not replace application tenant authorization.

rows.choose: Retain mesh concepts: proxy-based routing, telemetry, TLS, retries and traffic control.
rows.operations: Map each required capability to a supported Service Connect, Lattice or Kubernetes alternative and test migration behavior.
rows.watch: Support ended 30 September 2026; console/resources are no longer available. Do not select it for a new deployment or assume a replacement offers every feature.

rows.choose: HTTP/HTTPS ingress and health-based routing to compatible service targets.
rows.operations: Choose scheme, subnets, listeners, TLS/certificates, target type, security groups, health checks and deregistration behavior. awsvpc/Fargate task targets use IP.
rows.watch: An ALB does not grant workload IAM permissions. Match network mode and target registration; drain old targets and verify health before retiring tasks.

rows.choose: Private connectivity to supported service APIs or endpoint services through interface endpoints.
rows.operations: Configure endpoint subnets, security groups, private DNS, endpoint policy and the destination’s IAM/resource policy.
rows.watch: Endpoint existence does not imply authorization or access to all APIs. EKS management endpoints do not carry Kubernetes API traffic; S3 gateway endpoints have a different routing model.

rows.choose: Define network placement, routing and reachability for tasks, nodes, ingress and private dependencies.
rows.operations: Separate ingress from egress. Validate route tables, NAT/endpoints, DNS, security groups, subnet addresses and supported network-policy enforcement.
rows.watch: Private subnet placement is not complete isolation. Preserve DNS and required dependencies with deny policies; shared kernels and data access need additional controls.

rows.choose: DNS names, supported routing/health policies and tested regional application cutover.
rows.operations: Plan independent regional images, application stacks and data recovery, then validate domains, records, certificates, health signals and client caches.
rows.watch: DNS routing does not replicate images/data or promote a database. A hostname is not a literal A-record IP value; use the record type/alias supported by the target.

rows.choose: Manage eligible public or imported TLS certificates for supported service integrations.
rows.operations: Validate domain ownership, certificate Region/attachment requirements, renewal and hostname coverage for the selected endpoint.
rows.watch: A certificate does not create private reachability or workload authorization. Regional custom-domain behavior must be tested per service.

rows.choose: Issue private certificates for supported service-to-service TLS, including Service Connect.
rows.operations: Scope issuance/CA access, infrastructure roles and required managed secret permissions; monitor certificate lifecycle and cost.
rows.watch: Private certificate issuance and trust do not by themselves enforce tenant data permissions; TLS support is integration-specific.

rows.choose: AZ-scoped block volumes for supported EC2-backed Kubernetes workloads.
rows.operations: Use compatible CSI driver/identity, StorageClass or static PV, access mode and AZ-aware scheduling. Plan reclaim policy, snapshots and restore.
rows.watch: No EBS-backed Pod volumes on EKS Fargate. AZ scope and access mode matter; do not turn them into a universal one-Pod-per-volume claim.

rows.choose: Shared filesystem access from compatible workloads.
rows.operations: Configure mount targets, NFS security paths, access points/permissions and supported CSI provisioning. Match backup and recovery requirements.
rows.watch: EKS Fargate supports eligible static provisioning; dynamic persistent-volume provisioning is not supported for Fargate workloads. Filesystem sharing still requires tenant authorization.

rows.choose: Compatible high-performance shared filesystem workloads with supported EKS integration.
rows.operations: Install compatible CSI components and identity; validate node/kernel support, subnet/security paths, topology and filesystem lifecycle.
rows.watch: The Lustre CSI driver is not supported on Fargate. A generic StorageClass does not make every compute/backend combination compatible.

rows.choose: Supported ONTAP filesystem/protocol requirements and Kubernetes provisioning integrations.
rows.operations: Validate selected CSI/Trident integration, storage virtual machines, credentials, access modes, network and data lifecycle.
rows.watch: Different contract from Lustre. Current documented ONTAP CSI integration is not compatible with EKS Hybrid Nodes; validate driver and compute explicitly.

rows.choose: Object storage, including ECR image-layer download paths and supported application data.
rows.operations: For private ECR pulls, provide required S3 connectivity plus separate ECR API/registry paths. Scope bucket/endpoint/IAM policy and encryption access.
rows.watch: S3 gateway endpoint connectivity is not a substitute for ECR authentication or registry connectivity. Objects are not generic Pod POSIX volumes.

rows.choose: Authorize workload, startup and infrastructure AWS API operations.
rows.operations: ECS task role, execution role and host instance profile are distinct. EKS IRSA uses scoped OIDC trust; supported Pod Identity uses association/agent.
rows.watch: Kubernetes RBAC authorizes cluster operations separately. Pod Identity is not supported on EKS Fargate; restrict metadata access and broad node-role inheritance.

rows.choose: Retrieve supported startup/runtime credentials and managed certificate secrets.
rows.operations: Scope secret/KMS access and network paths. ECS injection happens at task start; rotate and replace tasks or implement safe runtime refresh.
rows.watch: Rotating a secret does not rewrite a running container’s environment. Keep credentials out of images/logs and test refresh failures.

rows.choose: Protect eligible image repositories, secrets and persistent data at rest.
rows.operations: Validate key policy, service integration, grants and cross-account/Region key choices before pull, mount and restore workflows.
rows.watch: A decryption permission does not replace repository, secret or filesystem authorization. Key availability can affect startup and recovery.

rows.choose: Task/Pod/application logs, metrics, alarms and supported Container Insights.
rows.operations: Connect symptoms to scheduling, capacity, image pull, IAM, network, health checks and application readiness. Configure log drivers/agents, permissions, network path and retention.
rows.watch: Healthy infrastructure metrics alone do not prove tenant authorization or application correctness. Collect events, rollout state and negative-test evidence too.

rows.choose: Supported external-host management and ECS Anywhere registration/control dependencies.
rows.operations: Install/maintain required agents and IAM, validate supported operating systems and service connectivity; retain local recovery access.
rows.watch: It does not transfer hardware/patching ownership to AWS. Running tasks and regional management availability have different disconnect behavior.

rows.choose: Adjust supported ECS service desired task count using configured policies.
rows.operations: Target tracking, step, scheduled and predictive scaling serve different demand patterns. Set min/max, metrics and cooldowns; coordinate with host capacity. Predictive scaling uses historical cycles and should be evaluated in forecast-only mode first.
rows.watch: It does not directly add unmanaged EC2 hosts. Deployment state, capacity shortages, image startup and health timing can delay usable capacity.

rows.choose: Scale supported EC2 host fleets used by container capacity.
rows.operations: Coordinate launch templates, AMIs, instance roles, AZ capacity, lifecycle/draining and the selected ECS/EKS capacity integration.
rows.watch: Adding hosts does not automatically change application desired tasks/replicas. Scale-in must respect compatible termination and disruption handling.

rows.choose: Managed application data with a deliberate regional/global-table consistency model.
rows.operations: Keep image replication, application rollout, table replication, authorization and traffic recovery as separate tested controls.
rows.watch: Global tables do not deploy containers or route SDK traffic automatically. Validate consistency mode and cross-tenant partition/key authorization.

rows.choose: Share supported namespaces/service-network resources across AWS account boundaries.
rows.operations: Configure supported resource shares, principals/organization permissions, acceptance where needed and underlying service associations.
rows.watch: Resource sharing does not replace caller IAM, network reachability or application authorization. Verify feature and Region eligibility.

rows.choose: Route supported operational events and trigger finite tasks with a supported scheduling integration.
rows.operations: For scheduled work, select EventBridge Scheduler or a supported rule pattern, execution role, target/task network configuration, retries and dead-letter handling.
rows.watch: A successful schedule trigger is not successful application completion. Finite tasks need completion/error monitoring and idempotency; continuous service desired-count behavior solves a different problem.

title: API front doors and real-time service choices

rows.choose: Feature-rich managed APIs needing supported usage plans, validation, stage cache, WAF, private endpoints or canary releases.
rows.operations: Choose endpoint type, deployment/stage, integration, caller authorization and backend permission independently. Use compatible OpenAPI definitions and request/response mapping.
rows.watch: Buffered payload 10 MB; backend Lambda 6 MB may constrain earlier. Qualify timeout by endpoint/transfer mode. REST feature support is not HTTP API feature support.

rows.choose: A leaner RESTful API when its lower-feature operating model meets the requirement.
rows.operations: Supported JWT/IAM/Lambda authorization, compatible Lambda/HTTP/AWS integrations, private backend options and optional automatic deployments.
rows.watch: Maximum integration timeout 30 seconds; payload 10 MB. No REST stage cache, usage-plan API keys, resource policies, private API endpoints, REST canary or native WAF feature parity.

rows.choose: Persistent bidirectional applications such as chat, collaboration or live notifications.
rows.operations: Manage connect/message/disconnect routes, trusted connection/user associations, compatible integrations and signed HTTPS backend callbacks.
rows.watch: Frame 32 KB/message 128 KB; connection 2 hours and idle 10 minutes. Reconnect, stale state and missed updates need handling; socket persistence is not durable message history.

rows.choose: A typed GraphQL contract assembling selected fields from compatible data sources, with supported real-time subscriptions.
rows.operations: Define schema, resolver logic, caller/field authorization, tenant/item predicates and scoped data-source IAM. Monitor resolver cost/fan-out.
rows.watch: GraphQL schema alone does not enforce every tenant boundary or implement offline synchronization. Subscription delivery follows its own authorization/filtering and mutation semantics.

rows.choose: Managed real-time publish/subscribe event APIs with supported channel authorization.
rows.operations: Use the Events API/channel contract and compatible publishing/subscribing clients; validate auth, message sizing, recovery and limits.
rows.watch: A separate product contract from GraphQL resolvers and mutation-linked subscriptions. Do not assume identical client protocol, payload or synchronization behavior.

rows.choose: A simpler HTTP endpoint when supported IAM or intentional public access fits the requirement.
rows.operations: Configure URL auth, resource policy, qualified function and compatible response mode. Since October 2025 new URLs require both InvokeFunctionUrl and InvokeFunction permission.
rows.watch: No automatic API Gateway feature set. NONE is unauthenticated access with an effective public resource policy, not a private user identity boundary.

rows.choose: HTTP routing across compatible Lambda and other target groups in a hybrid service architecture.
rows.operations: Listener rules select target groups; grant the service permission to invoke the qualified function. Validate the ALB event/response contract and supported WAF controls.
rows.watch: Lambda target request body 1 MB/response JSON1 MB; no WebSocket upgrade for that target. Same account/Region and one function per target group; network SG egress is not Lambda invoke authorization.

rows.choose: Event-triggered compute with compatible runtime/packaging and externalized durable state.
rows.operations: Tune memory/CPU, timeout, temporary storage, concurrency, IAM, source integration, retries and idempotent writes. Benchmark startup and downstream capacity.
rows.watch: Ordinary invocation 15 minutes,128–10,240 MB memory;1,769 MB≈one vCPU. Async, sync and poll-based sources have different failure contracts. Warm environment state is not durable.

rows.choose: Supported EC2 compute characteristics under Lambda-managed infrastructure operations.
rows.operations: Select compatible capacity provider, instance/workload configuration and permissions; validate concurrent worker model, billing, network and source support.
rows.watch: Eligible async and ESM invocation timeout 90 minutes, with MQ/DocumentDB exceptions. Do not apply every standard per-environment or cost assumption to this model.

rows.choose: Supported checkpointed multi-step application code with waits and recovery.
rows.operations: Use supported SDK/runtime and deterministic replay/step behavior; validate checkpoints, external side effects, retries and workflow-level limits.
rows.watch: Long wall-clock workflow duration is not one uninterrupted long-running invocation. General multi-service orchestration comparison continues in Module 14.

rows.choose: Automated Lambda alias traffic shifting with supported deployment modes, hooks, alarms and rollback.
rows.operations: Publish compatible versions and configure all-at-once, linear or canary policies. Retain old compatible code/data for recovery.
rows.watch: API Gateway stage deployment is a separate control. Completed deployment status alone does not prove correctness or data compatibility.

rows.choose: Infrastructure-as-code definition of supported serverless functions, APIs and deployment preferences.
rows.operations: Transform/package/deploy supported templates and required permissions; version changes and inspect generated infrastructure and deployment configuration.
rows.watch: SAM is a framework, not an inline runtime hop. Native feature support, deployment safety and secrets handling still need validation.

rows.choose: Store compatible Lambda container deployment artifacts by immutable image identity.
rows.operations: Build a Lambda Runtime API-compatible image, scope repository access and keep dependencies patched; retain proven rollback digests.
rows.watch: A ZIP deployment does not go through ECR. Image packaging is not permission to run an arbitrary always-on web server under standard Lambda semantics.

rows.choose: Compatible long-running or arbitrary container services that fit an orchestration/compute contract better.
rows.operations: Choose ECS service/task model and EC2/Fargate compute as taught in Module 12; plan networking, roles, health, rollout and capacity.
rows.watch: Container compute has a different operational/billing model. Packaging a service image does not make it a compatible Lambda runtime.

rows.choose: Compatible container tasks or Pods when that orchestration/compute contract fits better than standard Lambda.
rows.operations: Use supported ECS/EKS configurations, runtime resources, networking, roles, storage and rollout policies as taught in Module12.
rows.watch: Fargate is a compute option, not the orchestrator. ECS/EKS support differs; a long-running container remains subject to its selected platform and capacity constraints.

title: Supporting services in a serverless application path

rows.choose: Objects, thumbnail inputs/outputs, direct large uploads and eligible failed-invocation archives.
rows.operations: Scope bucket/key access and KMS; constrain presigned requests; configure event filters, browser CORS where needed and completion checks.
rows.watch: Events can repeat; prevent output recursion. Object writes and metadata writes are separate. Response streaming does not enable API request streaming.

rows.choose: Durable application/session state, idempotency records, image metadata and trusted connection associations.
rows.operations: Choose keys, conditional writes, consistency and capacity deliberately; process Streams through its poller/retry contract.
rows.watch: DynamoDB state does not make a Lambda environment or WebSocket durable. Enforce tenant data predicates; TTL cleanup is asynchronous.

rows.choose: Supported relational dependencies or eligible AppSync Aurora/Data API integrations.
rows.operations: Validate private reachability, database grants, connection capacity and supported Data API/engine/Region features. Use a compatible proxy when justified.
rows.watch: Network access, IAM and database login/data permission differ. A burst of Lambda clients can overload connections; an API timeout does not extend DB capacity.

rows.choose: Buffer event work and support compatible poll-based Lambda processing or failure retention.
rows.operations: Set visibility, retention, source permissions, retry/DLQ policy, batching and idempotency; use supported partial-batch responses.
rows.watch: Queue-trigger polling is not the Lambda async invocation queue. Function destination/DLQ support uses the specified standard queue contract, not arbitrary FIFO substitution.

rows.choose: Fan out events to independent consumers and supported async/DLQ/destination paths.
rows.operations: Configure topic/subscription policies, raw/enveloped payload shape, delivery retries and subscriber processing separately.
rows.watch: Standard SNS destination message size 256 KB can reject a larger invocation record. Topic delivery and successful business processing are distinct.

rows.choose: Replayable ordered-per-shard stream processing through supported Lambda event mappings.
rows.operations: Coordinate partitions/shards, source retention, batching, concurrency, checkpoints and failure age/retry behavior.
rows.watch: A poison record can affect progress; retries can repeat processing. Lambda scaling does not remove source throughput or downstream bottlenecks.

rows.choose: Route supported events or invoke qualified functions on an explicit schedule.
rows.operations: Scheduler execution role, timezone/window, retries and failed-delivery retention differ from handler code outcomes; use appropriate rule or Scheduler contract.
rows.watch: Schedule delivery success is not function business success. Bounded retries and idempotent side effects remain necessary.

rows.choose: Supported device-rule routing into Lambda processing.
rows.operations: Authenticate devices, authorize rule actions and scope Lambda resource permission to the intended source; validate event format and retries.
rows.watch: An IoT event trigger has its own producer/permission contract. It is not automatically an HTTP API integration or stream poller.

rows.choose: User-pool authentication, compatible JWTs/groups and supported user-pool Lambda triggers.
rows.operations: Validate issuer, audience/token type, expiry, scopes/groups and the selected API authorizer. Apply field/item authorization after authentication.
rows.watch: Cognito trigger timing/retry behavior differs from S3 async invocation. A valid token or group does not authorize every tenant record.

rows.choose: Execution evidence, access logs, alarms, latency and concurrency diagnosis.
rows.operations: Grant log-write permissions, set retention and correlate safe request/event identifiers. Use product-specific metrics, Logs subscription formats and log-delivery paths.
rows.watch: Default Lambda service log delivery does not prove application SDK network reachability. REST/HTTP API logging features differ; sensitive body logs can expose credentials.

rows.choose: Distributed trace analysis with supported API/Lambda service tracing and instrumentation.
rows.operations: Use current compatible OpenTelemetry instrumentation and required trace permissions; correlate downstream spans with logs and latency.
rows.watch: SDK/daemon maintenance began 25 February 2026, support ends 25 February 2027. That timeline is not retirement of the X-Ray service.

rows.choose: Supported OpenTelemetry instrumentation/collection for traces and observability.
rows.operations: Select a supported language/distribution/export path, sampling and permissions; validate network and telemetry cost.
rows.watch: Instrumentation is not a new application data hop; a dependency span must represent the actual caller, not an invented S3-to-database call chain.

rows.choose: Authorize API callers, function invocation and dependency operations through different identities/policies.
rows.operations: Scope identity/resource policies, integration roles, execution roles and source conditions; sign supported AWS requests with SigV4.
rows.watch: Caller token/IAM permission does not become a backend role automatically. Explicit denies, cross-account gates and tenant data authorization still matter.

rows.choose: Retrieve supported runtime/database credentials without embedding secrets in images or source.
rows.operations: Scope secret/KMS permissions and network access, use safe caching/refresh and validate rotation behavior.
rows.watch: Environment variables and logs are not an unrestricted secret distribution channel. Rotated credentials require compatible client refresh.

rows.choose: Protect eligible function configuration, object data and archives through supported encryption integrations.
rows.operations: Validate key policy, grants and required decrypt/data-key actions in producer/consumer/recovery accounts.
rows.watch: Encryption permission is separate from function invoke, bucket, queue or database permission; key availability can affect recovery.

rows.service: Amazon VPC · NAT and private networking
rows.choose: Private dependency access and deliberate egress identity/reachability.
rows.operations: Configure subnet routes, DNS, security groups, endpoints and NAT/IGW where needed. Place an EIP on the supported egress NAT, not Lambda.
rows.watch: Public subnet attachment alone does not give Lambda internet access. Keep database, NAT and endpoint branches separate in the actual path.

rows.choose: Supported private API/service endpoint reachability from compatible networks.
rows.operations: Configure execute-api endpoint DNS/SG/endpoint policy and REST resource/method authorization; validate cross-account/connected-network use.
rows.watch: A private API frontend and a VPC-link private backend are different directions. Endpoint existence is not access to every API or dependency.

rows.choose: Supported ALB/NLB targets behind current API Gateway private integrations.
rows.operations: Choose compatible VPC link version, same-account ownership where required, listener/security/TLS and stage-path mapping.
rows.watch: REST VPC link V2 support is broader than legacy V1. An ALB backend does not imply every API Gateway product supports every private target type.

rows.choose: Edge delivery/cache behavior in front of a compatible Regional API or the managed edge-optimized REST path.
rows.operations: Configure origin, cache identity, TLS and response/idle timeouts deliberately; separate regional API deployments and data recovery.
rows.watch: An edge entry point is not multi-Region backend recovery. Cache identity must not expose private tenant data.

rows.choose: Custom-domain DNS and tested routing between independent regional deployments.
rows.operations: Use supported alias/CNAME mappings, health signals and client DNS/reconnect behavior; validate certificates and backend readiness.
rows.watch: DNS does not deploy code, replicate data or promote a database. Source illustrative TTL is not a permanent universal service value.

rows.choose: Eligible API/ALB TLS certificates and custom-domain integrations.
rows.operations: Validate names, ownership, renewal and region attachment: edge-optimized API certificate us-east-1; Regional certificate in the API Region.
rows.watch: A certificate does not authorize invocation or create private networking. Select supported DNS mapping and mTLS configuration separately.

rows.choose: Supported web-request filtering for REST API stages, ALB or CloudFront designs.
rows.operations: Choose the supported attachment point, rule scope, logging and false-positive testing; correlate blocked requests with application evidence.
rows.watch: Direct REST WAF integration is not an HTTP API feature. WAF complements authentication and tenant/data authorization.

rows.choose: Supported direct API workflow start and multi-service orchestration.
rows.operations: Scope integration StartExecution or supported operation, validate input/response mode and distinguish intake from workflow completion.
rows.watch: Detailed workflow types, retries and orchestration are covered in Module 14. Removing a pass-through function does not make an async workflow synchronous.

rows.choose: Supported relational GraphQL/data access through eligible Aurora/Data API configurations.
rows.operations: Validate engine/Region/Data API availability, resolver request mapping, IAM, secret/KMS access and database grants.
rows.watch: AppSync does not bypass the Data API or database security contract. A compatible relational data source is not generic direct SQL access to any database endpoint.

rows.choose: Supported REST API access-log delivery and buffered delivery to compatible destinations.
rows.operations: Configure the supported log destination and role, buffering, transformation, failed-record handling and delivery monitoring.
rows.watch: REST access-log Firehose support is not HTTP API monitoring parity. Delivery buffering adds latency and does not replace function/request logs or trace evidence.

rows.choose: A compatible AppSync search data source or asynchronous derived search view.
rows.operations: Validate supported AppSync data-source configuration, resolver request/response mapping, IAM/domain or collection access policies, network reachability and index design.
rows.watch: A search index can lag its authoritative source. GraphQL field selection does not remove search authorization, shard/capacity limits or backfill/reconciliation requirements.

title: Queues, topics, event buses and brokers

rows.choose: Buffer and decouple asynchronous work.
rows.operations: Consumers pull/delete messages; choose Standard or FIFO, visibility, retention, DLQ.
rows.watch: Standard at least once and best-effort ordering; FIFO orders by message group.

rows.choose: Fan out a publication to independent subscriptions.
rows.operations: Topic/subscription filter, retry, delivery policy, IAM and KMS.
rows.watch: No durable consumer backlog; SNS FIFO eligible endpoints have ordered delivery.

rows.choose: Route events by patterns to rules and targets.
rows.operations: Bus/resource policy, target role, retry/DLQ, archive and replay.
rows.watch: Target invocation acceptance is separate from downstream handler completion.

rows.choose: Preserve supported broker protocols in a migration.
rows.operations: Choose ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ, broker sizing, network, users and HA.
rows.watch: IBM MQ/TIBCO need adapter or client/protocol migration.

rows.choose: Orchestrate a durable sequence of tasks and decisions.
rows.operations: State machine role, execution history, Retry/Catch, Standard/Express.
rows.watch: Workflow execution contract does not guarantee exactly-once external effects.

rows.choose: Invoke a target at one time or on cron/rate.
rows.operations: Time zone, flexible window, execution role, retry and SQS DLQ.
rows.watch: Target delivery retry is distinct from processing success.

rows.choose: Connect supported polling source to a target.
rows.operations: Optional filter and enrichment; role and source checkpoint behavior.
rows.watch: Retry and ordering behavior depend on source.

rows.choose: Deliver SNS publications to analytics/storage path.
rows.operations: SNS subscription role, Firehose buffering and destination policies.
rows.watch: SNS-to-Firehose path is not SNS directly writing to S3.

rows.choose: Trigger simple SNS fanout or use EventBridge integration.
rows.operations: S3 notification configuration and destination permission.
rows.watch: Choose EventBridge for richer event-pattern routing and target options.

rows.choose: Choose FIFO for per-group order and deduplication; Standard for high-scale unordered work.
rows.operations: Message group, deduplication ID/window, queue type and consumer idempotency.
rows.watch: FIFO does not make all business effects exactly once.

rows.choose: Choose FIFO for ordered eligible subscription delivery.
rows.operations: Topic type, message group and eligible endpoints.
rows.watch: Synchronous Lambda subscription to FIFO topic is not the FIFO path; use SQS bridge.

rows.choose: Give every subscriber an independent durable queue.
rows.operations: Queue policy allows source topic ARN; filters and consumer DLQ.
rows.watch: Each queue has independent backlog and failure.

rows.choose: Recover failed target delivery after bounded retry.
rows.operations: Target retry policy, SQS DLQ and queue permissions.
rows.watch: A successful target API call does not prove application processing.

rows.choose: Replay selected historical events for controlled recovery.
rows.operations: Archive pattern/retention and replay bus scope.
rows.watch: Replay can re-trigger matching rules; require idempotent consumers.

rows.choose: Wait for approval or external asynchronous job.
rows.operations: Protect token, SendTaskSuccess/Failure, heartbeat and timeout.
rows.watch: Activity worker and callback task have distinct contracts.

rows.choose: Route selected publications to a Firehose stream.
rows.operations: Subscription and delivery role, transform/buffer and destination access.
rows.watch: Endpoint support and payload limitations must be checked.

rows.choose: Correlate asynchronous request and reply through two queues.
rows.operations: Correlation ID, expiration, response queue and independent workers.
rows.watch: Neither synchronous RPC nor exactly-once reply by default.

title: Edge delivery, acceleration and private origins

rows.choose: Deliver HTTP(S) content and APIs through AWS edge with optional cache.
rows.operations: Distribution, behavior, origin, cache/origin-request policies, TLS, WAF and logs.
rows.watch: Cache key and TTL determine sharing and staleness; dynamic content can still use the edge.

rows.choose: Provide static anycast entry for TCP/UDP to healthy regional endpoints.
rows.operations: Listener, regional endpoint groups, health, traffic dials and endpoint weights.
rows.watch: No HTTP object cache; client-IP preservation depends on endpoint type and configuration.

rows.choose: Resolve DNS names with routing and health-aware policies.
rows.operations: Hosted zone, records, TTL, health checks and routing policy.
rows.watch: DNS caching/failover is not equivalent to fixed-IP anycast or edge object caching.

rows.service: Amazon S3 REST origin with OAC
rows.choose: Keep origin objects private behind CloudFront.
rows.operations: OAC SigV4, bucket SourceArn policy, KMS policy where required.
rows.watch: Viewer signed URL and origin OAC solve different access boundaries.

rows.choose: Serve S3 static website behavior including redirects.
rows.operations: CloudFront custom HTTP origin and appropriate public website access.
rows.watch: OAC/OAI cannot apply to S3 website endpoint; origin connection is HTTP.

rows.choose: Route dynamic HTTP(S) requests to application targets.
rows.operations: Publicly reachable ALB, CloudFront managed prefix list, secret origin header and listener rule.
rows.watch: Private ALB targets are possible; the ALB endpoint must be reachable by CloudFront standard custom-origin path.

rows.choose: Reach private ALB, NLB or EC2 origin in VPC private subnets.
rows.operations: Configure VPC origin and CloudFront-managed network connectivity; assess documented restrictions.
rows.watch: Different from the ordinary public custom-origin path and its prefix-list/header controls.

rows.choose: Fail eligible reads to a secondary origin.
rows.operations: Primary/secondary origins, configured failover codes and timeouts.
rows.watch: GET/HEAD and configured cached OPTIONS only; no POST/PUT failover.

rows.choose: Grant restricted access to one file/path with signed policy.
rows.operations: Trusted key group public key, application private signer and expiry/IP policy.
rows.watch: Unlike S3 presign, viewer checks happen at CloudFront before cache/origin.

rows.choose: Grant restricted access to multiple files without changing URLs.
rows.operations: Trusted key group, cookie policy and viewer access.
rows.watch: Signed URL takes precedence when both URL and cookies are present.

rows.choose: Grant a specific S3 request under the signer’s permission.
rows.operations: SigV4 principal credentials and expiry; S3 evaluates request.
rows.watch: Does not automatically provide CloudFront caching or edge authorization.

title: Caching, edge code and access choices

rows.choose: Run lightweight JavaScript at viewer request/response.
rows.operations: Published LIVE version, cache behavior association, compute utilization and runtime.
rows.watch: No origin events, network/file access or request body; KVS requires runtime 2.0.

rows.choose: Run Node.js/Python at viewer or origin event when richer code is needed.
rows.operations: Publish version in us-east-1; CloudFront replication, permissions and quotas.
rows.watch: Origin events occur on misses; viewer event combinations with Functions are restricted.

rows.choose: Choose cache key and TTL for object variants.
rows.operations: Headers, cookies, query strings, min/default/max TTL.
rows.watch: Forwarded values need not all enter cache key; avoid cache fragmentation or leaks.

rows.choose: Forward selected viewer values to origin without cache-key variation.
rows.operations: Headers, cookies and query strings forwarded to origin.
rows.watch: If origin response varies by a value absent from key, cached response may be shared incorrectly.

rows.choose: Remove cached objects under stable URLs.
rows.operations: Path/wildcard and deployment validation.
rows.watch: Versioned URLs often give more predictable release behavior.

rows.choose: Allow/block distribution access by country.
rows.operations: GeoIP country list and access policy.
rows.watch: Country location is approximate; not user authentication.

rows.choose: Trade serving-edge coverage for cost.
rows.operations: All, 200 or 100; assess traffic geography and current price schedule.
rows.watch: Fewer edge regions can increase latency; no fixed price claim.

rows.choose: Return a branded page/status for selected origin errors.
rows.operations: Error mapping, page path and Error Caching Minimum TTL.
rows.watch: A viewer-friendly status can hide origin failure from simplistic monitoring.

rows.choose: Distribute TCP/UDP to regional healthy endpoints.
rows.operations: Listener, Region group, dial, endpoint weights and health.
rows.watch: Dial percentage applies to traffic already directed to that Region.

rows.choose: Preserve source IP for supported endpoint types.
rows.operations: Endpoint type, enabled setting and security group/WAF controls.
rows.watch: Defaults and NLB/EIP behavior vary; validate network inspection implications.

title: Streaming and event transport service comparison

rows.choose: Retain ordered records for independent consumers and replay.
rows.operations: Partition keys, shard or on-demand capacity, retention, KCL/Lambda consumers and enhanced fan-out.
rows.watch: Order is per shard; hot partition keys and shared read limits need monitoring.

rows.choose: Buffer, optionally transform and deliver records to supported destinations.
rows.operations: Sources, Lambda transform, size/time hints, S3 backup, destination retry and dynamic partitioning.
rows.watch: Delivery is not a replayable stream; Redshift delivery stages through S3.

rows.service: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
rows.choose: Run continuous stateful stream analytics.
rows.operations: Event-time windows, joins, checkpoints, parallelism, source and sink permissions.
rows.watch: Checkpointed state and external side effects need separate failure and idempotency design.

rows.choose: Use Kafka protocol and ecosystem clients with managed brokers.
rows.operations: Provisioned or Serverless mode, topics, partitions, replication, consumer groups, VPC and security.
rows.watch: Broker management does not remove client, offset, poison-record and capacity decisions.

rows.choose: Decouple asynchronous workers with a queue.
rows.operations: Visibility timeout, redrive/DLQ, Standard or FIFO, consumer scaling.
rows.watch: A processed message is deleted; queue semantics differ from stream replay.

rows.choose: Push notifications and fan out to subscriptions.
rows.operations: Topics, filtering, subscription policies, SQS durable fan-out.
rows.watch: Subscriber delivery and downstream processing success are separate.

rows.choose: Store mutable keyed operational records.
rows.operations: Key design, read/write capacity, conditional writes, TTL and Streams when needed.
rows.watch: A table is not a message transport or historical event log.

rows.choose: Store durable objects and lake datasets.
rows.operations: Prefix layout, lifecycle, encryption, access control and event notifications.
rows.watch: An object store is not a queue; downstream processing needs explicit triggers.

title: Batch, lake and analytics service comparison

rows.choose: Schedule container jobs on eligible compute.
rows.operations: Job definition, queues, dependencies, compute environments, retries and IAM/network access.
rows.watch: Multi-node parallel jobs require EC2, not Fargate or Spot.

rows.choose: Run Spark, Hadoop and supported big-data engines.
rows.operations: EC2 clusters, EMR Serverless or EMR on EKS; primary/core/task roles and storage.
rows.watch: Cluster HDFS is transient; use S3 for durable datasets.

rows.choose: Discover metadata and run managed ETL.
rows.operations: Crawlers, Data Catalog, Spark/Python jobs, connections, bookmarks and permissions.
rows.watch: A crawler describes data; an ETL job transforms it.

rows.choose: Serve modeled analytical SQL and BI concurrency.
rows.operations: Provisioned or Serverless, COPY, WLM, Spectrum, snapshots and KMS access.
rows.watch: A snapshot copy needs restore and endpoint cutover; not instant failover.

rows.choose: Query lake data in S3 with serverless SQL.
rows.operations: Catalog tables, workgroups, results bucket, partitions, columnar files and connectors.
rows.watch: Scan cost and latency depend on layout and query shape.

rows.choose: Build analyses and publish dashboards.
rows.operations: Dataset access, SPICE refresh or direct query, author/reader permissions and row/column security.
rows.watch: Dashboard sharing and data-level security are distinct.

rows.choose: Subscribe to governed third-party datasets.
rows.operations: Provider terms, entitlements, delivery method, updates and consumption permissions.
rows.watch: Subscription access and downstream AWS usage charges are separate.

rows.choose: Find supported software vulnerabilities and EC2 network exposure.
rows.operations: Enable resource scan types; monitor eligibility, exclusions, inventory and coverage.
rows.watch: Scanning does not patch a workload or prove exploitation.

rows.choose: Detect suspicious activity with threat intelligence and behavior signals.
rows.operations: Foundational sources plus resource-specific protection plans; delegated administration.
rows.watch: Runtime Monitoring requires a supported agent; coverage and enablement are regional.

rows.choose: Discover sensitive data in supported S3 objects and review bucket posture.
rows.operations: Automated discovery or scoped jobs, identifiers, format and IAM/KMS access.
rows.watch: No content finding does not establish that every object was analyzed.

rows.choose: Investigate relationships and activity around a security finding.
rows.operations: Behavior graph, principal/IP/resource pivots and time windows.
rows.watch: Investigation context requires interpretation; it does not enforce containment.

rows.choose: Prioritize and respond to correlated security issues.
rows.operations: Enable contributing services and organize exposure response workflows.
rows.watch: Do not equate its enablement or configuration with Security Hub CSPM.

rows.choose: Analyze external, internal or unused access and validate policies.
rows.operations: Create the appropriate analyzer and scope; review findings and policy checks.
rows.watch: Potential policy access and observed API activity are different evidence.

title: Configuration, security data and audit evidence

rows.choose: Record resource configuration, relationships and compliance history.
rows.operations: Recorder, resource scope, rules, aggregator and optional remediation.
rows.watch: A rule evaluation does not deny the original API request.

rows.choose: Evaluate security controls and posture against enabled standards.
rows.operations: Required Config recording, control settings, central configuration and findings.
rows.watch: The current Config setup path differs when both Hub and CSPM are enabled.

rows.choose: Centralize supported security logs and events for investigation.
rows.operations: OCSF records in S3; source scope, retention, rollup and subscriber permissions.
rows.watch: A data lake is not a replacement for a detection or remediation workflow.

rows.choose: Organize control evidence and produce assessment reports.
rows.operations: Framework/control mappings, automated/manual evidence, reviewers and report selection.
rows.watch: Evidence collection does not certify customer compliance.

rows.choose: Obtain AWS and eligible third-party assurance reports and agreements.
rows.operations: Select relevant report, period and scope; observe sharing terms.
rows.watch: Provider assurance does not demonstrate the customer operated its controls.

rows.choose: Retain API activity evidence for audit and investigation.
rows.operations: Trail or event data store scope, event selectors, archive and access controls.
rows.watch: Data event coverage and retention require deliberate configuration.

rows.choose: Route matching finding and compliance events.
rows.operations: Event patterns, target permissions, retries and dead-letter handling.
rows.watch: Routing an event does not mean the target action completed.

rows.choose: Execute a controlled remediation runbook.
rows.operations: AutomationAssumeRole, parameters, approvals, current-state checks and execution logs.
rows.watch: Stale Config results can initiate remediation after a resource has already changed.

rows.choose: Validate or enrich events and perform scoped response logic.
rows.operations: Execution role, idempotency, failure handling and evidence capture.
rows.watch: Untrusted finding fields must not become unrestricted resource/action inputs.

rows.choose: Coordinate response stages, approvals, retries and verification.
rows.operations: State transitions, task credentials, timeouts and human decision integration.
rows.watch: Workflow success should include verification of the security outcome.

rows.choose: Image and video labels, faces, text, content moderation and tracking.
rows.operations: Select Image or Video API, threshold and region; protect images and face collections.
rows.watch: Moderation labels and confidence are not a final safety decision; consent and human review matter.

rows.choose: Extract printed text, handwriting, forms, tables, expense or identity fields from document images/PDFs.
rows.operations: Synchronous/asynchronous APIs vary; validate confidence and preserve source version.
rows.watch: OCR text alone does not guarantee correct typed fields or totals.

rows.choose: Speech to text for subtitles, calls and searchable audio.
rows.operations: Configure language identification, custom vocabulary and optional PII redaction.
rows.watch: Redaction is not automatic; protect original audio and transcripts.

rows.choose: Synthesize spoken audio from text or supported SSML.
rows.operations: Use voice/engine, pronunciation lexicons and SSML controls where supported.
rows.watch: A lexicon handles pronunciation, not translation or speech recognition.

rows.choose: Translate text and localize applications or documents.
rows.operations: Choose supported language pair and terminology; review quality.
rows.watch: It neither transcribes audio nor synthesizes speech.

rows.choose: ASR/NLU chatbot or voice bot intent and slot capture.
rows.operations: Design intents, fallback and Lambda fulfillment; integrate Connect for calls.
rows.watch: Lex interprets intent; Connect operates the contact center.

rows.choose: Cloud contact center, call routing and contact flows.
rows.operations: Connect flows can invoke Lex, Lambda and integrated CRM.
rows.watch: Avoid the PDF’s unqualified percentage savings claim.

rows.choose: General text language, entity, key phrase, sentiment, syntax and topic insight.
rows.operations: Select suitable real-time or batch API and evaluate output quality.
rows.watch: General NLP is not clinical PHI extraction.

rows.choose: Clinical text entities and PHI detection.
rows.operations: Use supported medical APIs such as DetectPHI; protect source/derived PHI.
rows.watch: Entity identification does not by itself establish clinical validity or compliance.

rows.choose: Real-time tailored product, media or outreach recommendations.
rows.operations: Prepare interactions/items; serve through recommendation API and ingest events.
rows.watch: Cold start, consent, relevance and bias need explicit evaluation.

rows.choose: Existing managed natural-language enterprise document search.
rows.operations: Index supported data sources; tune relevance, freshness and access.
rows.watch: Closed to new customers 30 July 2026; evaluate Bedrock Knowledge Bases for new solutions.

rows.choose: Prepare, train, tune, deploy and monitor custom ML models.
rows.operations: Select data pipeline, training job, endpoint or batch mode and controls.
rows.watch: Training/validation quality and deployment operating model are your responsibility.

rows.choose: No-code predictive models, including time-series forecasting.
rows.operations: Import data, build/evaluate model and generate predictions.
rows.watch: Assess fit against specialized Forecast legacy workload and pricing.

rows.choose: Existing managed time-series forecasting.
rows.operations: Historical time-series plus related data; existing users continue.
rows.watch: Closed to new customers since July 2024; avoid source’s unqualified 50% improvement claim.

rows.choose: Managed foundation model inference for generative AI.
rows.operations: IAM/model access, chosen model, runtime, safeguards and logging by Region.
rows.watch: Model invocation is not automatically grounded in private documents.

rows.choose: Managed retrieval over private sources for RAG and cited answers.
rows.operations: Ingest/sync sources, choose managed or customer-managed infrastructure, scope access.
rows.watch: Check retrieval permission, freshness and citations; generated answer can still be wrong.

rows.choose: Configure supported input/output content and sensitive-information checks.
rows.operations: Attach guardrail to supported inference/KB flow; inspect interventions.
rows.watch: Does not authorize tools, protect every modality or apply to embedding/reranking models.

rows.choose: Managed orchestration of model, action groups and knowledge bases.
rows.operations: InvokeAgent uses agent alias, service role, optional guardrail, trace and session context.
rows.watch: Agent chooses a possible action; it does not create business authorization.

rows.choose: Define typed tool/API contract and parameter elicitation.
rows.operations: Fulfill through Lambda or return control to your application; optional user confirmation.
rows.watch: Validate parameters and current state in executor; handle retries and denial.

rows.choose: Ground answers in indexed private evidence.
rows.operations: Scope source ingestion and query access; trace retrieved data.
rows.watch: Retrieved text is untrusted data and cannot grant tool access.

rows.choose: Run bounded business logic for agent action group.
rows.operations: Lambda resource policy allows Bedrock invocation; its execution role separately scopes downstream calls.
rows.watch: Avoid broad privileges and duplicate side effects.

rows.choose: Host custom agent workload with managed runtime.
rows.operations: Protect inbound access and configure appropriate observability.
rows.watch: Distinct from the Bedrock Agents managed orchestration service.

rows.choose: Inbound and outbound agent identity and credential management.
rows.operations: Configure IAM/JWT or OAuth patterns and scoped outbound providers.
rows.watch: Caller authentication is not blanket authority for external tools.

rows.choose: Expose and govern tool targets through a central gateway.
rows.operations: Protect entry and attach fine-grained policy where supported; retain downstream enforcement.
rows.watch: Default denial and scope must be tested, including absent caller context.

rows.choose: Supported input/output content, topic, word and sensitive-information checks.
rows.operations: Attach to supported inference or agent flows and evaluate interventions.
rows.watch: Guardrails do not authorize tool calls or replace IAM.

rows.choose: Check a response against modeled policy logic.
rows.operations: Inspect contradiction/assumption feedback and policy coverage.
rows.watch: Does not stop prompt injection; no streaming, English US and modeled-variable limits per current docs.

rows.choose: Recorded supported API activity and principal context.
rows.operations: Correlate request IDs and Region with trace and application decision record.
rows.watch: API activity alone does not capture full prompt, approval rationale or tool result.

rows.choose: Request end-user confirmation for selected actions.
rows.operations: Present proposed function, target and parameters; deny stops action.
rows.watch: A confirmation should precede execution and the app still validates permissions.

rows.choose: Durable workflow that pauses for a reviewer decision.
rows.operations: Use task token, authorized callback, timeout and reject branch.
rows.watch: A notification or click alone is not a secure approval record.

rows.choose: Troubleshoot orchestration, retrieval and action steps.
rows.operations: Enable trace and protect sensitive parameters/observations.
rows.watch: A trace explains path selection; it is not a preventive control.

rows.choose: Runtime and gateway metrics, logs and traces.
rows.operations: Resource-specific telemetry and log destinations need configuration.
rows.watch: Do not assume all resource types produce all signals by default.

rows.choose: Native declarative infrastructure templates and stack lifecycle.
rows.operations: Validate template, create change set, use scoped deployment role and inspect events.
rows.watch: Change set previews possible replacements but does not guarantee update success.

rows.choose: Concise serverless resources, local CLI testing and deployment.
rows.operations: Transform SAM declarations into CloudFormation resources; CodeDeploy can shift Lambda alias traffic.
rows.watch: Local tests do not prove deployed IAM, network or integration behavior.

rows.choose: Define infrastructure with programming-language constructs.
rows.operations: Synthesize templates/assets; bootstrap environment as needed; deploy through CloudFormation.
rows.watch: Inspect generated IAM and replacement effects, not only source code.

rows.choose: Approved self-service products for teams.
rows.operations: Admin versions product and portfolio; IAM and launch role govern provisioning.
rows.watch: Modern products can also use supported Terraform artifacts; not every product is just a CloudFormation template.

rows.choose: Preview template update and likely replacement actions.
rows.operations: Review add/modify/remove, parameters, IAM and data-bearing resources before execute.
rows.watch: Preview cannot prove success or exact downstream effect.

rows.choose: Retain, snapshot if supported, or delete resource on stack removal.
rows.operations: RDS DBCluster and standalone DBInstance have Snapshot default; S3 delete needs empty bucket.
rows.watch: Does not govern the old physical resource on replacement.

rows.choose: Control old physical resource when stack update replaces it.
rows.operations: Select Delete, Retain or Snapshot as supported; assess new endpoint and data migration.
rows.watch: Different event from removing a resource from a stack.

rows.choose: Deploy stack instances to chosen accounts and Regions.
rows.operations: Self-managed roles or Organizations service-managed permissions; configure target, order and tolerance.
rows.watch: Automatic OU enrollment requires service-managed configuration and monitoring.

rows.choose: Adopt an existing supported resource into stack ownership.
rows.operations: Manual import uses whole-stack template, identifier, DeletionPolicy, IMPORT change set.
rows.watch: Auto-import requires static name and Retain/RetainExceptOnCreate; run drift detection after.

rows.choose: Compare supported actual properties with template expectations.
rows.operations: Run per stack/resource; inspect differences and plan safe reconciliation.
rows.watch: Drift detection does not prevent manual changes or cover unsupported properties.

rows.choose: Extend stack lifecycle to unsupported or external operations.
rows.operations: Provider handles Create/Update/Delete, callback, physical ID, retries and rollback.
rows.watch: Missing response or non-idempotent Delete can block cleanup.

rows.choose: Policy-as-code validation of JSON/YAML templates and related data.
rows.operations: Run rule tests and cfn-guard validate in CI, preserve evidence.
rows.watch: A local check is not a deployed enforcement gate unless wired in.

rows.choose: Evaluate selected operations at CloudFormation/Cloud Control boundary.
rows.operations: Configure target, actions, filters and warn/fail mode; activate in intended accounts/Regions.
rows.watch: Warn does not block; fail mode and scope determine enforcement.

rows.choose: Resolve protected secret value during CloudFormation operations.
rows.operations: Use scoped read/KMS access and runtime rotation integration.
rows.watch: Rotation does not automatically cause a new stack operation.

rows.choose: Provision approved product using a defined role.
rows.operations: Role scope is per product/portfolio association; end-user portfolio access is separate.
rows.watch: Launch role can still be too broad despite product approval.

rows.choose: Inspect or alter constructs during synthesis using a reusable aspect.
rows.operations: Apply at app, stage or construct scope; synth and inspect generated CloudFormation.
rows.watch: An aspect is a build-time control and does not protect templates deployed outside that CDK app.

rows.choose: Set maximum account permissions for principals in member accounts.
rows.operations: Attach to root, OU or account; test explicit denies with IAM policies.
rows.watch: SCP does not grant permissions and does not inspect a CloudFormation template.

rows.choose: Assess deployed resource compliance and optionally remediate.
rows.operations: Record supported resources; evaluate rules with appropriate service role and scope.
rows.watch: Detection after deployment does not prevent the initial noncompliant create.

rows.choose: Reference encrypted parameter values in templates and at runtime.
rows.operations: Use ssm-secure dynamic references and scoped SSM/KMS read permissions.
rows.watch: Version and rotation behavior differ from Secrets Manager; a value change does not itself redeploy a stack.
